extra.message: The HTTP query parameters red, green, and blue are passed directly to eval() (lines 32-34) without any sanitization. An attacker can supply arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. /cwe95/rgbToHex?red=require('child_process').execSync('id')) that is executed server-side, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

User-supplied parameter foo is used verbatim as a filesystem path in fse.readJsonSync(req.query.foo). There is no allowlist, path canonicalization, or traversal check, so an attacker can read arbitrary JSON files on the server (e.g. /cwe73/read?foo=/etc/... or traversal sequences), an external control of file name/path allowing arbitrary file read.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The query parameter text is concatenated into an HTML response and sent with res.send() without any encoding or escaping. A crafted request like /cwe79/echo?text=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> causes the payload to be rendered and executed in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

Both the response header name and its value are taken directly from user input (req.query.key and req.query.value) and passed to res.append(). An attacker can inject CRLF sequences into the header value to perform HTTP response splitting / header injection, and can also overwrite or spoof arbitrary headers (e.g. security headers), enabling cache poisoning, session fixation, or XSS via injected headers.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The query parameter text is reflected verbatim into the HTTP response body via res.send(req.query.text) (Express sends strings as text/html). Untrusted attacker-controlled content is echoed without encoding, which can be used for reflected XSS; the endpoint is annotated CWE-201 (Information Exposure Through Sent Data) since arbitrary reflected data is sent back to the client unencoded.

cwe: CWE-201: Information Exposure Through Sent Data

extra.message: User-controlled query parameter text is concatenated into the destination URL passed to res.redirect(). The attacker-controlled portion lands in the redirect Location value; combined with CRLF injection in the value (and depending on the Node/Express version) this allows response splitting / redirect to attacker-chosen content. The endpoint is annotated CWE-601 (open redirect) and lets a remote user steer the redirect target string.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Attacker-controlled query parameter foo is deserialized with serialize.unserialize() from the node-serialize package with no integrity/authentication check. node-serialize executes immediately-invoked function expressions embedded via _$$ND_FUNC$$_, so a payload such as {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function (){...}()"} achieves arbitrary remote code execution on the server.

The query parameter foo is passed directly to child_process.exec(), which executes its argument through a shell (/bin/sh). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via metacharacters (e.g. /cwe78/childprocess?foo=pwd%3Bcat%20/etc/passwd or using ; | & $()), leading to full OS command execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
